issues.description: Class name and file contents mismatch: the exercise expects a public class named 'Farm' (see UML in the problem statement and the solution implementation), but the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares 'public class AnimalFarm' and contains duplicated/malformed content (including an illegal 'package' declaration at line 10 inside a method). This prevents the intended mapping between problem, template, and solution and will cause compilation failures (Main and tests expect a class named Farm and a valid Farm API).
issues.suggestedFix: Replace or fix src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java in the template so it matches the problem statement and solution conventions: (1) Declare 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' at the top and remove any nested/duplicate 'package' statements; (2) Rename the public class to 'Farm' so the public class name matches the file name; (3) Remove duplicated/malformed blocks and provide a clean stub that compiles, e.g. 'public class Farm { private List<Animal> animals; public Farm() { animals = new ArrayList<>(); } public List<Animal> getAnimals() {...} public void setAnimals(List<Animal>) {...} public void addAnimal(Animal) {...} public void feedAllAnimals() {...} public void singFarmSong() {...} private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal) {...} }' — keeping method bodies either empty or minimal println stubs is acceptable for pedagogical reasons, but the file must be syntactically valid and use the identifier 'Farm'. This aligns the template with the UML and solution and prevents compilation errors for students and tests.
